text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
_ A Sunday Times investigation shows that private schools which charge heavily are a rip-off and that more children in public schools pass examinations than those in private schools.

- Voluntary repatriation of 6,000 Liberian refugees in Nigeria will begin after the installation of a democratically-elected government in that country in August, says the chairman of the National Commission for Refugees, Abdulkadir Mohammed.
- Oil minister Dan Etete unfolds new measures to address the crippling fuel shortage that has gripped oil-producing Nigeria.
- Banks scramble to open offices in Nigeria's capital Abuja.

- There are indications that military ruler General Sani Abacha may have shelved an undeclared ambition to contest next year's presidential election to transform into an elected leader, political sources say.
- Chief executives of banks form a lobby group to influence policy formulation and execution.
- The discovery of crude oil deposits in parts of Bayelsa state in the southeast is threatening to spark a communal crisis as two local councils each claim ownership of the oil-rich territory.
